title: unified-rollouts-canary-ab-shadow-autorollback-improvements
author: Maya Patel
release_notes:
- Improve autorollback decision engine to support composite metrics and quorum-based rollbacks.
- Add staged probing and quarantine stages for shadow/canary traffic.
- Add telemetry (Prometheus + traces) and e2e tests for rollout safety.
- No breaking changes to the rollout configuration API; opt-in for new policies.
description:
Context: This PR enhances the unified rollouts service to reduce noisy/incorrect rollbacks and provide safer progressive deployments across canary, A/B, and shadow traffic modes. Motivation is from recent incidents where noisy single-metric spikes triggered broad rollbacks and caused unnecessary churn (see ENG-3421 and ENG-3490).

What this changes (high level):
- Introduces a composite-metric evaluator that aggregates multiple signals (latency p95/p99, error rate, model-quality regression score) with configurable weights and a quorum threshold.
- Adds staged probing and quarantine stages: a probing stage that samples additional traffic to validate regressions before escalation, and a quarantine stage that isolates suspect variants without impacting a full rollback immediately.
- Extends the autorollback workflow to support conditional weighted canary adjustments and automated shadow quarantining for degraded model variants.
- Adds observability: new Prometheus metrics (rollout_evaluator_score_total, rollout_quarantine_events_total, rollout_probing_success_ratio) and tracing hooks for rollback decisions. Dashboards and alert rules included.
- Adds e2e stability tests and integration tests for the probe/quarantine paths.
- Adds safety guards: minimum evaluation window, minimum sample size, and cooldown backoff to prevent oscillation.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests updated and added; [x] Integration/e2e tests added; [x] Docs updated; [x] Linear links included; [x] Telemetry dashboards and alert rules added.

Technical notes: The composite evaluator is implemented as a pluggable policy under rollout/policies/composite_evaluator.go. It exposes a lightweight DSL for metric weighting and quorum configuration. Probing is implemented as a short-lived sampling route that increases sample rate for the candidate variant and records a probe verdict to the rollout controller. Quarantine is an automated transition that reduces candidate weight to zero for production traffic but keeps it available for probing and manual inspection.

Compatibility: Existing rollout CRDs and API surface are unchanged; the new evaluator is opt-in via the rollout.policy.name = "composite-evaluator" and rollout.policy.params. Ops can enable the policy per-namespace or per-customer.

Related: previous PRs on unified rollouts auto-rollback improvements and observability (see references in repo).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Generally LGTM. A couple of questions: 1) how do we avoid false positives when only a single metric glances above threshold; 2) can we expose a per-customer override for quorum thresholds?

Maya Patel (author): Good points. The composite evaluator includes a quorum clause (configurable) so a single-metric spike won't trigger a violation unless quorum satisfied. I've added per-customer config support in pkg/rollouts/config/defaults.yaml and documented examples in composite_policy_example.yaml.
Zara Nguyen: Tests look solid, but e2e runs were flaky on CI previously. Can you add a stability guard (retry/backoff) to the e2e pipeline?
Maya Patel (author): Added stability guard to e2e workflow and increased probe sampling window to reduce flakiness. Reran CI and fixed the intermittent race in controller shutdown.
Diego Martinez: Observability additions are great. Please ensure metric labels include rollout_id and customer_id for scoping in dashboards.
Maya Patel (author): Done — rollout_id and customer_id added to all new metrics.

Zara Nguyen: Approving — verified dashboards and smoke-tested in staging.
